question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[X{Y}^{2}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}8xy,\, & 0\le x,\,0\le y,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1; \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=x{y}^{2}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x,\,0\le y,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154787/assets/dfa15482cfa0e8fdc9e98b05a71d2b64a89b3886da44f6966fee9f1b5e096eef.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X{Y}^{2}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}x{y}^{2}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}x{y}^{2}\cdot 8xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-2{x}^{4}+{x}^{6})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{2}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{7}{x}^{7}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =2[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{7}] \\  & =\frac{16}{105}.\end{aligned}
$$
